name: Caswell County Courthouse
customer: Architecture fans, courthouse counters, history travellers
unique: An 1861 courthouse in the Italianate style with arched windows, a bracketed cornice and a clock tower, standing on the square in a town that was laid out in 1792 and has never been much bigger than it was then.
buzz: Courthouse people put it on their short list for the tower and the brickwork. Everyone else is in town for the history and walks in without knowing what they are looking at.

name: Yanceyville Historic District
unique: A county seat of brick storefronts and antebellum and Victorian houses around the courthouse square, in a county that was the richest in North Carolina before the tobacco economy collapsed and left the buildings standing.
buzz: The architecture is better than the town's reputation suggests and the streets are quiet. People come for the courthouse and stay to walk the blocks behind it.

name: Milton and the Dan River
unique: A tobacco town of brick warehouses and houses above the Dan River, once a shipping point for leaf that went downriver to the mills, with a landing where paddlers put in below the shoals.
buzz: Small, quiet and full of old commercial buildings that have not been fixed up or torn down. Paddlers know the river access and everybody else drives through without stopping.

name: Louisburg Historic District
unique: A courthouse town on the Tar River with blocks of eighteenth and nineteenth century houses, a main street of brick storefronts and a college campus that has been part of the town since the 1780s.
buzz: It is one of the older towns in the piedmont and it feels like it. The walkable grid and the river at the bottom of the hill are the reasons to stop.

name: Louisburg College
unique: A small Methodist college founded in the 1780s with a main building of brick and columns on a hill above the town, the oldest chartered college in North Carolina still operating under its founding charter.
buzz: The campus is small and shaded and the main hall is the photograph. Locals walk it in the evening and the college is the reason the town has a rhythm.

name: Tar River
unique: A piedmont river running below Louisburg with wooded banks, gravel shoals and public accesses, wide enough to paddle and shallow enough to wade when the water is low.
buzz: Anglers fish it for bass and catfish and paddlers run it after rain. There are no facilities, so it is the kind of river you bring two cars for.

name: Greene County Museum
company: Greene County Arts and Historical Society
unique: A county museum in Snow Hill with changing exhibits on the tobacco, cotton and peanut farms around it, the schools and churches of the county, and the African American music heritage of the coastal plain.
buzz: Volunteers run it and the exhibits change, which means there is always a reason to go back. It is small and free and the staff know the families.

name: Snow Hill Downtown
unique: A main street of nineteenth and early twentieth century storefronts around a courthouse, including a rare cast iron fronted building, in a county seat that has kept its commercial block intact.
buzz: The cast iron facade is the thing architectural people come for and most visitors walk right past it. The town is quiet and the buildings are the attraction.

name: Contentnea Creek
unique: A blackwater creek winding through the coastal plain farmland, with cypress and gum along the banks, a public access at Snow Hill and fishable water all the way to the Neuse.
buzz: Local paddlers use it as a close to home float and anglers fish the fallen timber. It is quiet, free and has no facilities beyond a ramp.

name: Hyco Lake
cost: Free, camping and marina fees extra
dates: Year round, best May to October
unique: The largest lake in Person County, built by Carolina Power and Light for cooling and now a recreation lake of more than seven hundred acres with a county park, campground and marina on the shoreline.
buzz: Families camp at the park and fish off the piers and boaters use it as a quiet alternative to the bigger lakes. The county runs it and the prices reflect that.

name: Kirby Theater
unique: A restored 1920s theater on Roxboro's uptown main street, run as a community arts venue with live music, films and local productions under an ornate ceiling.
buzz: The room is the draw and the tickets are cheap. People drive from Durham for the shows and are surprised by the town's main street.

name: Person County Museum of History
unique: A museum in a 1920s house covering the tobacco, textile and farming history of the county, with period rooms, farm tools and the records of the families who built Roxboro.
buzz: Volunteers give the tour and the period rooms are the part people remember. It is small and free and the garden is worth the walk.

name: Mayo River State Park
unique: A new state park along the Mayo River with a mountain access that climbs to a view over the valley, river access for paddling and trails through hardwood forest that was farm and mill land a century ago.
buzz: It is one of the newer parks in the system and still quiet. The Mayo Mountain overlook and the river access are the two reasons people go.

name: Reidsville Downtown
unique: A main street of early twentieth century commercial buildings and churches in a town that grew on tobacco and textiles, with a historic district that includes some of the best brickwork in the county.
buzz: Quieter than it was when the mills ran, but the buildings are intact and the town is working on the rest. People walk it on the way to the park.

name: Rockingham County Courthouse Square
unique: A rural county seat of a few hundred people with an 1900s courthouse on a knoll, a Confederate monument and a handful of buildings, surrounded by fields rather than a town.
buzz: It is one of the smallest county seats in the state and that is the curiosity. The courthouse and the view across the fields are the whole visit.

name: Somerset Place
unique: The 1830s Collins family house on Lake Phelps with a full plantation landscape of kitchen, dairy, stables and slave quarters, interpreted around the more than eight hundred enslaved people who made the place work, with their names and families documented.
buzz: The interpretation is the best part, with the enslaved community named and mapped rather than mentioned. People come for the house and leave talking about the quarters and the records.

name: Pettigrew State Park
unique: A park on the shore of Lake Phelps, the second largest natural lake in North Carolina, formed on an ancient marine terrace, with cypress and swamp forest, a canoe trail and wintering tundra swans.
buzz: The lake is shallow, tea colored and full of stumps, which keeps the powerboats away and makes it a paddler's lake. Winter brings thousands of swans and the campground is quiet.

name: Plymouth Downtown and the Albemarle
unique: A river town on the Roanoke where the Confederate ironclad Albemarle was built and later sunk, with a waterfront, a museum and a downtown that has rebuilt after hurricanes and floods more than once.
buzz: The ironclad story is the reason history people stop and the riverfront is the reason everybody else does. The town is small and proud of both.

name: Gates County Courthouse
unique: An 1836 Greek Revival courthouse of hand made brick on the square in Gatesville, one of the oldest courthouses in continuous use in North Carolina and the center of a county that has stayed almost entirely agricultural.
buzz: It is a two minute stop and the brickwork is worth it. Courthouse chasers count it among the state's best small ones.

name: Roanoke River National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Bottomland hardwood along the Roanoke protected for migratory birds and black bears, with the river as the main road in, cypress and tupelo in the sloughs and a paddle trail that threads the refuge.
buzz: Paddlers see bears and otters in the mornings and birders come for the spring migrants. There are almost no facilities, which is why the river is quiet.
